Write-off under the allowance method: Dr Allowance for Doubtful Accounts, Cr Accounts Receivable.
Writing off an uncollectible account under the allowance method affects:
Neither Net Income nor Cash Realizable Value.
Cash Realizable Value of Accounts Receivable only.
Both Net Income and Total Assets.
Both A/R and the allowance fall by the same amount, so net realizable value and net income do not change.
The Direct Write-Off Method violates which accounting principle?
The direct write-off method records the expense when the account is written off, not in the period of the sale, so it violates matching.

Accounts Receivable has a balance of $400,000, and the Allowance for Doubtful Accounts has a credit balance of $3,000 before adjustment. Aging of receivables estimates uncollectible accounts to be $25,000. What is Bad Debt Expense for the period?
Required allowance 25,000; credit balance 3,000 already there, so expense = 25,000 − 3,000 = 22,000.
Using the facts in Question 64, suppose the Allowance for Doubtful Accounts had a DEBIT balance of $3,000 before adjustment. What is Bad Debt Expense?
Debit balance of 3,000 must be cleared too: expense = 25,000 + 3,000 = 28,000.
Cash Realizable Value of Accounts Receivable is calculated as:
Accounts Receivable minus Allowance for Doubtful Accounts
Accounts Receivable plus Allowance for Doubtful Accounts
Accounts Receivable minus Bad Debt Expense
Cash realizable value = accounts receivable − allowance for doubtful accounts.
When a previously written-off account is subsequently collected under the allowance method, how many journal entries are required?
Reinstate the account (Dr A/R, Cr Allowance), then record the cash collection (Dr Cash, Cr A/R): two entries.

What is the maturity date of a 60-day note dated July 10?
Days left in July = 21, plus 31 in August = 52, plus 8 in September = 60, so maturity is September 8.

Which method of estimating uncollectibles emphasizes the Balance Sheet (Cash Realizable Value)?
Percentage-of-receivables (aging) focuses on the balance sheet: the required allowance.
The party making the promise to pay on a promissory note is called the:
The maker is the party who signs the note and promises to pay.
Non-trade receivables include all of the following EXCEPT:
Amounts owed by customers from credit sales
Amounts owed by customers from credit sales are trade receivables, not non-trade.
Under the Direct Write-Off method, bad debt losses are recorded:
When an account is determined to be uncollectible.
In the same period as the related sale.
At the end of every month based on estimates.
Direct write-off records bad debt expense only when an account is determined to be uncollectible.
